# YM22: 水木明瑟 Shuimu Mingse, "A Stream and Trees and a Bright Lute"

Malone calls it Shui Mu Ming Se.

Wave 2 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM22` · Page: `/scenes/#YM22` · Row: `research/buildings/YM22-shuimu-mingse/`

## What it was

水木明瑟 Shuimu Mingse, north-east of 映水兰香: a three-bay hall built across a stream, where a European water device (泰西水法) drove fans inside the room, whence the name 风扇房 (S05 j81:35a; E1686, S361; E1685, S02). 文源阁, the library of 1774, was built just north-west of it (S05 j81:35b; S02 says on the site of rice fields and a double-roofed pavilion, E1685). Plaques by Qianlong and, 一溪清水引风凉, by Yongzheng (S05 j81:35a). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).

From the inventory row: **built** 雍正时期 (S42); **changed** Rice fields and double-roof pavilion in the album background replaced by 文源阁 1774 (S02 p.89); **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S02, S08, S42, S01).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Lyric of 1744 (to 秋风清): "用泰西水法引入室中以轉風扇泠泠瑟瑟非絲非竹天籟遙聞" (S05 j81:35a-b): water drawn into the room by the Western method turns the fans, with a clear sound, neither string nor flute, like the music of heaven.

### How later sources differ

The 1774 文源阁 changed the neighbourhood (S05 j81:35b); S01 labels 丰乐轩 in this scene (YM22-02), but S05 puts 丰乐轩 in 紫碧山房 (E2302): a tie to check.

## Gaps and wishlist

The water mechanism is not described in detail anywhere found; no dig of the stream channel.

### Open questions that name it

- **Q39. 丰乐轩 YM22-02.** S01 labels it in 水木明瑟; S05 j81:25a, poems of 1761 and 1767 (S201), S360 p.200 and S337 put it in 紫碧山房 (YM48-04), 647 m away (run). Two plaques, a wrong parent, or a name moved on the plan?
- **Q59. Twin claims to hold loosely.** 海晏堂 follows the Grand Trianon: Beurdeley 1971 p.68, repeated widely; Rabreau (S415 p.81) says its grounds would be sought in vain. No filiation of any Xiyang Lou building to a European print is proved. 安佑宫 YM17 仿寿皇殿 (S05 j.81 f.20b), but that hall had only 3 bays before 1749 (S422)
